name: Snow Peak
why: Niigata camping-gear maker from 1958 whose flame-resistant Takibi clothing became a line of its own; three US stores, Portland, Brooklyn and Seattle, taken private with Bain in 2024.
origin: Founded in 1958 in Niigata Prefecture, Japan (Tsubame-Sanjo area; HQ in Sanjo) by Yukio Yamai (founder) and Tohru Yamai CEO from 1980 and apparel founded by Lisa (Riie) Yamai after 2014.

onething.p: TAKIBI flame-resistant apparel (Hybrid Takibi Jacket); the house is best known for camping gear (titanium mugs, Takibi Fire & Grill)

notes.tech: Thread proposed 4 (2026-10-11): GORE-TEX (3-layer shell, waterproof down, SR-1 wading jacket, rain pants), PERTEX Quantum Air, PRIMALOFT insulation, Polartec Thermal Pro and High Loft, Teijin Octa lining, Conex aramid (Takibi Ripstop Vest), house TAKIBI flame-resistant fabrics (modacrylic blends, "Takibi Spec"), C0 (PFC-free) DWR — licensed (Gore, Pertex, PrimaLoft, Polartec, Teijin); TAKIBI flame-resistant fabric is the house spec ("Japan Fabric" on PDPs), mill not named; share of range about 24/111 styles (22%) carry a named technical fabric or the Takibi flame-res. Seated as proposed, pending ruling.
notes.craft: Thread proposed 2 (2026-10-11): Snow Peak names no apparel factory, maker or mill on any of the 111 men's product pages and owns no stated apparel facility; only 5 styles state a country (3 Japan, 2 Italy) and 7 more say "Japan Fabric". The dated Niigata/Tsubame-Sanjo heritage is real but belongs to the camping gear, not the clothing. Fabric descriptions are specific, which keeps it off a 1. Seated as proposed, pending ruling.

craft_evidence.owned: gear: Global Headquarters in Niigata (Sanjo) and Tsubame-Sanjo metal craftsmen named for gear on the history page; apparel: no owned factory stated
craft_evidence.mills: none named as mill; Teijin named as fibre/fabric maker on Octa (3) and Conex (1) styles = tech, not craft; "Calamai" in the Calamai Wool Fleece title (Made in Italy) may be a fabric name, not stated as a mill
craft_evidence.madein: 5/111 PDPs state a country (3 Made in Japan: Indigo C/N Jacket, Anorak, Pants; 2 Made in Italy: Calamai Wool Fleece Pullover and Jacket); a further 7 say "Japan Fabric"; all 111 PDPs read
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed: founded 1958 by Yukio Yamai in Niigata Prefecture (Tsubame-Sanjo metal craftsmen); apparel line launched by Lisa Yamai after she joined in 2014; US wholesale from 1999 (Gresham OR)
craft_evidence.process: partial: fabric construction described (triple weave, kasuri ripstop, pigment washing, yarn-dyed antique dyeing, recycled denim with Guatemalan yarn woven in Japan); no making process or factory documented for apparel
craft_evidence.reasoning: Snow Peak names no apparel factory, maker or mill on any of the 111 men's product pages and owns no stated apparel facility; only 5 styles state a country (3 Japan, 2 Italy) and 7 more say "Japan Fabric". The dated Niigata/Tsubame-Sanjo heritage is real but belongs to the camping gear, not the clothing. Fabric descriptions are specific, which keeps it off a 1.

ownership.owner: Snow Peak, Inc. (株式会社スノーピーク) taken private in a 2024 management buyout with Bain Capital: tender offer by BCJ-80 Inc. (parent BCJ-79 Inc., Bain Capital vehicles) ran 21 Feb-12 Apr 2024 at JPY 1,250/share; succeeded with 59.55% tendered (settled 19 Apr 2024), followed by share consolidation and TSE delisting; Tohru Yamai (14.21% before) expected to keep running the company and hold shares indirectly. Snow Peak USA is the US arm. Verified to the tender result; the delisting date itself was not read.
